channel.title: MFM Rounds
channel.description: A weekly peer-level digest of the most important new maternal-fetal medicine research, with Juno and Caspar.
channel.itunes:author: Juno & Caspar

item.title: Aspirin Does Not Erase the Risk Tier
item.description:
MFM Rounds, week of October 12th. The Lin paper is not about whether aspirin works. It's about who still develops preterm preeclampsia despite it — and whether we can identify those women at booking. The answer is yes, and the predictor is the same FMF risk tier we used to put them on aspirin in the first place. Which means the criteria we use to select women for aspirin and the criteria we use to surveil them afterward are not the same list. Most protocols are...

  5. 3:06 — Pivot and Round 1: Zeng — CSP Outcomes

  7. 4:39 — Round 3: Benuzzi — ML Ceiling for Term Stillbirth

  9. 6:12 — Close: Open Threads and Sign-Off


Follow-up links:
  • Determinants of preterm pre-eclampsia following low-dose aspirin prophylaxis: evidence from stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial in Asia - Multicenter RCT secondary analysis directly informing aspirin prophylaxis counseling and post-prophylaxis surveillance stratification
  • Adverse outcome in Cesarean scar pregnancy continuing into mid-to-late gestation: systematic review and meta-analysis - Quantifies catastrophic outcomes in expectant-managed CSP, supporting early intervention discussions
  • Postpartum Venous Thrombosis in Sweden: A Nationwide Family Study - Nationwide cohort supporting hereditary risk scoring for postpartum thromboprophylaxis decisions
  • Limits of Machine Learning for Predicting Stillbirth at Term: A Population-Based Cohort of 302,192 Pregnancies in Northern Italy - Large population study demonstrating ceiling effects of registry-variable ML models for stillbirth prediction
  • Diagnostic imaging of adnexal lesions in pregnancy: systematic review - Systematic review highlighting variable performance of IOTA models in pregnancy and lack of validated pregnancy-specific algorithms

item.title: Ultrasound After Delivery Accelerates Recovery
item.description:
MFM Rounds, week of October 19th. The headline is a multicenter double-blind RCT in postpartum care — Liu and colleagues, UOG 2026. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound, sham-controlled, hard endpoint. The result is real. The replication question is also real. From Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology, 2026: Liu and colleagues, a multicenter double-blind RCT — low-intensity pulsed ultrasound to facilitate uterine involution. LIPUS — non-thermal,...

Chapters:
  1. 0:00 — Cold Open: What This Week's Lead Paper Changes
  2. 0:47 — Headline: The Clinical Question and Why It Needs a Sham Control
  3. 1:34 — Headline: The Effect, the Numbers, and the Mechanistic Gap
  4. 2:22 — Headline: What Actually Changes in Practice
  5. 3:09 — Pivot and Round 1: Gulersen — Steroid Threshold
  6. 3:56 — Round 2: Komargodski — ADHD Medications in Pregnancy
  7. 4:43 — Round 3: Rao — Transabdominal Cerclage Indications
  8. 5:30 — Round 4: Foo — Preeclampsia Cardiovascular Phenotyping
  9. 6:18 — Close: What to Watch, What Is Still Unsettled


Follow-up links:
  • Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound to facilitate uterine involution: prospective multicenter study on clinical efficacy and mechanistic insights - First multicenter double-blind RCT showing LIPUS accelerates postpartum uterine involution and reduces complications versus sham
  • Changing practice: establishing a preterm birth risk threshold to guide antenatal corticosteroid administration - Proposes an evidence-based threshold to rationalize steroid administration and reduce unnecessary fetal exposure
  • Pregnancy and Offspring Outcomes After Prenatal Stimulant or Atomoxetine Exposure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis - Quantifies associations between prenatal ADHD medication exposure and adverse pregnancy outcomes for counseling
  • Transabdominal Cerclage: Who, When, How - Clarifies precise indications for TAC with RCT-level support for recurrent sPTB under 28 weeks after failed TVC
  • Pre-Eclampsia and Maternal Cardiovascular Function: Insights Into Pathophysiology and Care (Scientific Impact Paper No. 79) - RCOG guideline-level synthesis supporting cardiovascular phenotype-guided antihypertensive therapy in preeclampsia
